reason: Driven and measured, every layout fact holds. At 390 the owner bar is 162px of four ragged rows (.b-where alone at y48, .b-switch at y73, then the action wrapper wrapping again so Publish is orphaned at y158), and .b-spacer does occupy a real 102px slot at x=232 on the switch row (height 0, so 'visible' overstates it, but the wrap it forces is real). Nothing steps the hero down at phone width: [data-medium="full"] keeps .b-num at 148px and .b-when at 30px, so 'Saturday 3 October 2026' runs to two lines (78px) and the first .b-item sits at 1038px on an 844px screen in both owner-flight and owner-editing; at 768 it is 975px on 1024px, i.e. clinging to the bottom edge. Neither gate touches this - interaction-check only asserts no sideways scroll and no collisions at 390 - so it is not a restatement, it breaks no constraint, and it is a real defect on the device this product is opened on. BUT the fix as written is wrong on three counts, verified by applying it: (1) the three .b-act buttons are not children of .b-bar, they sit in an unclassed inline-styled flex div in render-b.js line 176, so `grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr)` puts all three inside one 86px cell - the bar goes from 162px to 232px, 'Add a moment' wraps to two lines, and the first item drops to 1108px. The fix makes the bar worse. (2) `.b-num` and `.b-when` in a media query lose to `[data-medium="full"] .b-num` on specificity, so neither hero step applies at all - measured font-size stays 148px/30px with the fix in place. (3) The stated target is unreachable from these rules: even with both hero steps forced to land, the first item only rises to 990px at 390, still below an 844px fold.
sharpenedFix: Two files, not one. In render-b.js `bar()`, give the actions wrapper a real class - replace the inline-styled div at the `owner-flight`/`owner-editing`/`owner-empty` call sites with `h("div.b-barActs", ...)` and move its flex rules into b.css. Then in b.css's existing `@media (max-width: 700px)` block: `.b-spacer { display: none; } .b-where { flex: 1 0 100%; } .b-barActs { display: grid; width: 100%; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 8px; } .b-barActs > .b-act { text-align: center; } .b-barActs > .b-act[data-primary="true"] { grid-column: 1 / -1; }` - measured at 390 this gives two equal secondaries on one row and Publish full-width beneath as a deliberate primary, no orphan, no squashed label, and it degrades correctly for owner-empty's single action. For the hero, the rules must out-specify the medium selectors: write them as `[data-medium="sheet"] .b-num, [data-medium="full"] .b-num, .b-num { font-size: 104px; }` inside the 700px block and the same three-selector form for `.b-when` (24px at <=700, 26px at <=900) - measured, that alone lifts the first item from 1038 to 990 at 390 and unwraps the date at 768. Set the acceptance target honestly: the first item cannot reach the first viewport at 390 from type and chrome alone, because 224px of the 1038 is the measure's real 16-day lead-in and 131px is the 'behind you' block riding above the measure inside .b-stick. If getting the first item above the fold at 390 is actually wanted, it is a small build, not a CSS tweak: split behindBlock() out of .b-stick so it can be ordered below the measure at <=700px. With that plus the two steps above the first item lands near 790px. Verify at 390 and 768 on owner-flight and owner-editing: bar height, no orphaned action, .b-when on one line, first-item top.
